observations: Photo is very dark/underexposed, taken at an angle.
Shape shows a deep, curved-back television cabinet consistent with a CRT (tube) TV, not a flat panel.
Vents and a glossy black plastic casing are visible on the back/side of the set.
Set sits on a tiled floor in what looks like a home interior; no power cable, remote, or screen face is visible.
No brand name, model number, or screen is visible or legible anywhere in the frame.

claims.evidence: No LG logo, label, or size marking visible anywhere in photo 0; only a dark rear/side view is shown.

claims.claim: The transformer is blown (i.e., it is not working)
claims.evidence: Cannot see internal parts or power-on test in photo 0; this is the seller's own description of the fault.

claims.evidence: The screen face is not shown at all in photo 0; also irrelevant/unusual phrasing for a CRT, which doesn't have 'pixels' in the LCD sense.

risks.risk: Unit confirmed non-functional by seller (blown transformer); true extent of damage (just transformer vs. other board damage) unknown.
risks.proof: A clear photo/video of the unit powering on or attempting to power on, plus an open-case photo showing the power board/transformer area.

risks.risk: Screen condition (claimed no dead pixels/lines) cannot be checked since this is a CRT with no screen shown.
risks.proof: A well-lit photo of the full screen face, ideally powered on or at least showing the tube clearly.
risks.if_unproven: priced as condition unknown, assume cosmetic/tube wear typical of an old CRT

risks.risk: Brand and screen size claim (LG, 29-inch) cannot be confirmed from any visible marking.
risks.proof: A clear, well-lit photo of the brand logo/nameplate and screen size label, typically on the front bezel or rear panel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unbranded/unconfirmed 29-inch-class CRT TV

risks.risk: Remote claimed included but not photographed; could be missing, wrong remote, or non-functional.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual remote next to the TV.
risks.if_unproven: priced as TV only, no remote

risks.risk: Overall cosmetic condition (cracks, burns, water damage) hidden by poor lighting and odd angle.
risks.proof: Multiple well-lit photos from front, back, and both sides in daylight.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming heavy cosmetic wear, worst case for an old, non-working CRT

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit photo of the brand/model/size label on the TV (usually rear panel or front bottom bezel).
Photo or short video attempting to power the TV on, to confirm the 'blown transformer' fault and rule out further damage.
Well-lit photo of the full screen face.
Photo of the remote control alongside the TV.
Photo of the open back panel showing the power supply/transformer area.
response.reason: The photo is dark and shows no readable brand/model/size, and the screen itself is never shown, but the seller's own words confirm the unit is non-working (blown transformer); this is enough to identify it generically as a CRT TV and price it at worst case as a non-functional, unconfirmed-brand set pending the listed proofs.
